title: NSS Feed Output Format: Sandbox Verdict Logs

blocks.text: The Sandbox verdict Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) feed specifies the data from the Sandbox verdict logs that the NSS sends to the security information and event management (SIEM) system. You can configure an NSS feed by including one or more fields. The fields and their values display in the NSS feed output.

blocks.item: View a sample Sandbox verdict log.

blocks.text: The following tables display information about the Sandbox verdict log fields and possible values for those fields.
The following are date and time fields:

table: The log time (i.e., when a transaction is logged by the Zscaler Nanolog)
The log time (i.e., when a transaction is logged by the Zscaler Nanolog) in integer format
The feed time (i.e., when a transaction is received by the NSS from the Nanolog)
Seconds (0–59) as recorded in the feed time (%s{rtime})
Minutes (0–59) as recorded in the feed time (%s{rtime})
Hours (0–23) as recorded in the feed time (%s{rtime})

The day of the month (1–31) as recorded in the feed time (%s{rtime})
The name of the month as recorded in the feed time (%s{rtime})

Year as recorded in the feed time (%s{rtime})
The time zone. This is the same as the time zone you specified when you configured the NSS feed.

The event time (i.e., when the Sandbox analysis response is processed by the Public Service Edge for Internet Access (ZIA)). The Public Service Edge sends the payload to the Sandbox for analysis at time X and processes the response from the Sandbox at time X+2, which is the event time.
The event time (i.e., when the Sandbox analysis response is processed by the Public Service Edge for Internet Access) in integer format

blocks.text: A SIEM can have parsing issues whenever a string field has non-printable or delimiter characters. For that reason, the Zscaler service has URL encoding for URL fields like URL, Referer, and Hostname. There are several other fields that have the same parsing issue, but URL encoding is not suitable. Such fields are encoded using Base64.
Turning on Base64 encoding for all supported fields might result in approximately a 20% drop in performance.

The Zscaler service hex encodes all non-printable ASCII characters that are in URLs when it sends logs to the NSS. Any URL character that is less than or equal to 0x20, or greater than or equal to 0x7F, is encoded as %HH. This ensures that your SIEM can parse the URLs that contain control characters. For example, a \n character in a URL is encoded as %0A, and a space is encoded as %20.
